verdicts.flaw_description: Rainfall in each plot's season 'ran a fifth higher than the year before' and 'every plot stood in the open, on no set watering schedule', so the extra water actually reached every plant and was not offset by controlled irrigation; a 20 percent rainfall increase is an alternative cause of the 8-13 cm height gains that fits all four plots.

Two of the four cases have measurement dates preceding the intervention: section One was 'issued 4 November' but completion was read 'by 27 September', and section Three was 'issued 5 June' but read 'by 28 April'. Those gains were recorded before the kit was ever handed out.

The timings 'cover the runs that stayed on the issued route' while 'about a sixth of each depot's runs left the issued route', so roughly 17 percent of runs are dropped from the measured averages. The excluded runs are exactly the ones that hit trouble and would be slowest, so the 5-9 minute improvement is an artifact of which runs were counted.

Absence figures 'cover the pupils on the revised timetable throughout' while 'about a fifth of each cohort spent weeks on the old timetable', so roughly 20 percent of each cohort is excluded from the numbers. Pupils absent enough to miss the switch are precisely the high-absence group being filtered out, which alone could produce the 4-7 percent drop.
